newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down, buying seen to fade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down, buying seen to fade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed marginally easier on Wednesday on modest shortcovering but the buying is seen fading towards the end of the week as players go away for their Christmas holidays, dealers said.
"Most people have already bought whatever they needed so I think this shortcovering is going to die down soon. Some of the trades posted today were done yesterday," a local rubber trader said.
"There was also a bit of speculative buying and switching being done by some traders between RSS3 and RSS1 rubber," another trader said.
The most active month was the July/September RSS3 contract with 2,175 tonnes traded. Volume on the April/June RSS1 contract reached 1,200 tonnes.
"By next week, this market will be asleep," one dealer said. At around 0945 GMT, March RSS3 was seen at 127.00-128.00 U.S. cents a kg compared with the previous 128.25 cents.
February RSS1 was seen at 178.00-180.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.28) a kg against 180.25 cents.
April/June TSR20 was seen at 175.00-176.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25-$1.26) a kg from 176.75 cents.
